definitions.explanation: Plants in general, especially the combination of grasses and trees that make up natural vegetation.

examples.japanese: {春|はる}になると{草木|そうもく}が{芽吹|めぶ}く。
examples.english: When spring comes, the plants begin to sprout.

examples.japanese: {庭|にわ}の{草木|そうもく}の{手入|てい}れをした。
examples.english: I tended to the plants in the garden.

examples.japanese: {草木|そうもく}も{眠|ねむ}る{丑三|うしみ}つ{時|どき}という{言葉|ことば}があるが、{真夜中|まよなか}の{静|しず}けさを{表|あらわ}す{表現|ひょうげん}だ。
examples.english: There's the expression 'the hour when even the plants sleep,' which describes the stillness of the dead of night.

notes:
A Sino-Japanese reading of {草|そう} (grass) + {木|もく} (tree). This is the on'yomi reading, used in more literary, formal, or set expression contexts. The same kanji can also be read {草木|くさき} (kun'yomi), which is the more colloquial reading.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {草木|そうもく}が{茂|しげ}る — vegetation grows thick
- {草木|そうもく}が{枯|か}れる — vegetation withers
- {草木|そうもく}が{芽吹|めぶ}く — plants bud/sprout
- {草木|そうもく}も{眠|ねむ}る — even the plants sleep (set phrase for dead of night)

RELATED READING:
- {草木|くさき} — the same kanji read with kun'yomi; more colloquial and used in everyday speech to refer to trees and grass. The そうもく reading is more literary.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {植物|しょくぶつ} — plants (botanical/scientific term); more formal and includes all plants, not just visible vegetation
- {緑|みどり} — greenery; focuses on the visual aspect of green plants
- {植生|しょくせい} — vegetation (ecological term); technical term for the plant life of a region
